observation.visible_scene: A dense green forest with a pale gravel/dirt trail running from the bottom-center toward the horizon. Tall, dark tree trunks line both sides of the trail and a leafy canopy fills the upper frame. Bright sunlight breaks through a gap in the canopy at the top-center, throwing dappled light-and-shadow patches across the trail surface.
visible_changes: The camera translates forward along the trail: the nearest left trunk drifts from mid-left toward the left edge (roughly x=170 at t=0 to x=60 at t=3.2) and the nearest right trunk drifts from right-of-center toward the right edge (roughly x=860 to x=960), so side trees slide outward past the frame as the viewpoint advances.
The trail's vanishing point and the sunlit canopy gap stay near the horizontal center throughout, consistent with forward motion aligned with the path rather than a pan.
Dappled shadow patches on the trail move toward the bottom of the frame (toward the viewer) as the camera advances, with new illuminated sections of path appearing further ahead.
The bright sun flare at the top-center grows slightly larger and more washed-out over the clip, and the overall foreground shading darkens a little as the viewpoint moves under denser canopy.

Tree trunks and foliage do not change shape or position relative to the ground; their apparent motion is due to camera translation, not object movement. Minor leaf-position differences between frames suggest light wind sway but are not clearly separable from camera shake.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the forward walk continues, stops, or turns after t=3.2 (the segment ends mid-motion).
What lies at the far end of the trail beyond the sunlit gap.
Whether the slight change in sun glare is exposure, canopy opening, or angle shift – the cause is not visible.
Any wind source or ground conditions outside the frame.
uncertain_details: Exact speed of the forward camera motion (no fixed ground reference is tracked).
Whether subtle canopy movement is wind or handheld camera shake.
Whether the apparent expansion of the top-center brightness is physical (camera approaching the gap) or photographic (auto-exposure).
